chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who stole, and the evidence was established against him: should we refer him so that his hand may be cut, while he is cut in other than its due limit? He said: “Yes, refer him.”

key_terms.ارْفَعْهُ: bring him forward or refer him to the authority
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: the legal proof or clear evidence
key_terms.حَدِّهِ: its proper legal limit or prescribed bound
key_terms.نَرْفَعُهُ: should we refer him to the authority or bring his case forward
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: his hand is cut as the prescribed punishment

ai.seo_question: If theft is proven by evidence, should the accused be brought forward for the hadd punishment?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a judicial ruling concerning theft after the legal proof has been established. Imam Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام affirms that the thief should be brought forward for the prescribed legal action.
